text: You put a mutable list in a HashMap as a key, then add an element to it. What happens?
choices: The entry becomes permanently unreachable — it cannot be retrieved or removed
An exception is thrown on the next lookup
The map updates its index automatically
explanation: It was filed in the bucket for its hash at insertion. Changing the hash sends the lookup to a different bucket, and the entry sits in the old one forever. Use immutable types as keys — which is a large part of why Map<String, ...> is so common.
